blogPosts.title: How Much Does a New Fence Cost in Drysdale in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the true cost of a new fence in Drysdale in 2026. We break down timber and Colorbond pricing, concrete footings, and site factors for Bellarine homeowners.
body: If you are a Drysdale homeowner planning a new fence, understanding the cost is the first step. In 2026, the average cost of a residential fence in Drysdale and the wider Bellarine Peninsula ranges from $150 to $350 per linear metre, depending on the material, height, and complexity of the job. Factors like the type of timber or Colorbond selected, the length of the fence line, site accessibility, and ground conditions all influence the final price. At Fencing Geelong & Bellarine, we provide free, fixed-price quotes that break down every cost so you can budget with confidence.

The choice of fencing material is the single biggest factor affecting your budget. Treated pine fencing, one of the most popular options in the Geelong region, typically costs between $150 and $220 per metre installed. Hardwood options like treated hardwood or Merbau sit higher, ranging from $200 to $300 per metre due to the premium timber quality. Colorbond fencing offers a mid-range to premium option, with prices generally falling between $180 and $280 per metre. These prices include galvanised fittings, concrete footings, and professional installation by a licensed contractor.

Concrete footings are a critical component of any quality fence installation in Drysdale. Given the Bellarine Peninsula's varied soil conditions, from sandy coastal ground to heavier clay soils, properly poured concrete footings are essential for long-term stability. The cost of concrete footings is typically included in your per-metre price when you engage a professional fencing contractor. However, if you are getting quotes, always confirm whether footings are included, as some contractors may quote a lower per-metre rate but charge extra for the concrete base work.

Several site-specific factors can affect the total cost of your fencing project in Drysdale. Sloping or uneven ground requires additional labour and sometimes stepped panels or custom cutting, which can add 10 to 20 percent to the base price. Restricted access to the fence line, such as narrow side passages or steep drops, may also increase costs due to the difficulty of moving materials. Fencing near the coast also benefits from upgraded galvanised or stainless steel hardware to resist salt corrosion, which adds a small premium but protects your investment for decades.

Property fencing in the Drysdale area often involves compliance with local council regulations. The Bellarine Peninsula falls under the Borough of Queenscliffe and the City of Greater Geelong, both of which have specific requirements for fence height, setback, and materials. Pool fencing, in particular, must comply with Australian Standard AS 1926, which sets strict rules for height, gate self-closing, and gap measurements. A reputable fence contractor in Drysdale will handle the permit process and ensure your new fence meets all relevant standards.

To get the best value for your fencing project, it pays to get multiple quotes from licensed local contractors. At Fencing Geelong & Bellarine, we encourage Drysdale and Bellarine homeowners to compare our detailed, itemised quotes against others. Our pricing includes all materials, labour, concrete footings, galvanised fittings, and a workmanship guarantee. We never charge for quotes, and there is absolutely no obligation. Contact us today to arrange a same-week on-site assessment and find out exactly what a new fence will cost for your Drysdale property.

blogPosts.title: Timber vs Colorbond Fencing on the Bellarine Peninsula: Which is Better?
blogPosts.excerpt: Timber or Colorbond? Compare both fencing materials for the Bellarine Peninsula's coastal conditions. We cover durability, cost, maintenance, and the best choice for Drysdale properties.
body: Choosing between timber and Colorbond fencing is one of the biggest decisions Drysdale and Bellarine Peninsula homeowners face when planning a new fence. Both materials have their strengths, and the best choice depends on your budget, aesthetic preferences, and how much maintenance you are willing to commit to. In the unique coastal environment of the Bellarine, where salt air, strong winds, and intense UV exposure are constant factors, making the right material choice is especially important. This guide compares timber and Colorbond fencing across every factor that matters for properties in the Geelong and Bellarine region.

Timber fencing has been the traditional choice in the Bellarine Peninsula for decades, and for good reason. Treated pine and hardwood options offer a natural, warm appearance that complements the coastal character of Drysdale properties. Timber fences can be stained, painted, or left to weather naturally to a silver-grey finish. The main advantages of timber are its natural look, ease of repair, and the ability to customise panel designs. However, timber requires regular maintenance, including staining or painting every two to three years, to protect against moisture, termites, and UV damage.

Colorbond fencing is manufactured from high-tensile steel with a durable baked-on paint finish, making it exceptionally resistant to the coastal conditions found across the Bellarine Peninsula. It comes in over 20 colours, from classic neutrals to modern bold tones, so you can match your home's style without the ongoing maintenance that timber demands. Colorbond does not rot, warp, or attract termites, and it holds its colour far longer than painted timber. For Drysdale homeowners who want a low-maintenance, long-lasting fence, Colorbond is often the preferred choice.

When it comes to durability in the Bellarine coastal environment, Colorbond fencing has a clear advantage. The steel construction resists the salt-laden winds that can accelerate timber degradation in Drysdale and surrounding suburbs. Colorbond panels are also wind-rated, with specific configurations designed to handle the strong gusts that sweep across the peninsula during storms. Timber fencing, while durable when properly maintained, is more susceptible to warping, swelling, and rot in high-moisture coastal conditions. For homes exposed to the worst of the Bellarine weather, Colorbond offers superior long-term performance.

Cost is always a consideration for Drysdale homeowners comparing timber and Colorbond fencing. Treated pine fencing typically costs between $150 and $220 per linear metre installed, making it the more affordable upfront option. Colorbond fencing generally ranges from $180 to $280 per metre installed, depending on the colour and profile chosen. While Colorbond has a higher initial cost, the savings on maintenance over 15 to 20 years often make it the more economical choice overall. Timber requires regular staining or painting, while Colorbond needs only an occasional wash with soapy water.

For Drysdale and Bellarine homeowners still deciding, consider the long-term value each material offers. If you love the natural look of timber and are happy to invest in regular maintenance, timber fencing can look beautiful for decades. If you prefer a modern, zero-maintenance fence that will look the same in 20 years as it does on installation day, Colorbond is the smarter investment. At Fencing Geelong & Bellarine, we supply and install both timber and Colorbond fencing across the Bellarine Peninsula. Contact us for a free on-site quote and we will help you choose the best option for your Drysdale property.

blogPosts.title: Best Fencing Materials for Drysdale's Coastal Conditions
blogPosts.excerpt: Drysdale's coastal conditions demand the right fencing materials. Learn which timber species, Colorbond profiles, and hardware perform best on the Bellarine Peninsula.
body: Living in Drysdale on the Bellarine Peninsula means enjoying stunning coastal views, fresh ocean breezes, and a relaxed outdoor lifestyle. However, these same coastal conditions that make the area so desirable also create significant challenges for fencing. Salt-laden winds, high humidity, intense UV radiation, and occasional severe storms all take a toll on fence materials over time. Choosing the right fencing material for Drysdale's coastal conditions is essential to ensure your fence lasts for decades without costly repairs or premature replacement.

The coastal environment of the Bellarine Peninsula is classified as a high-corrosion zone by Australian building standards. This means that standard steel components will rust rapidly unless they are properly treated or galvanised. For fencing, this makes galvanised steel fittings and hardware absolutely essential. At Fencing Geelong & Bellarine, we use only premium galvanised fittings and bugle batten screws on every project, ensuring that the structural connections of your fence are protected against the salt air that is a constant factor in Drysdale and surrounding suburbs.

Colorbond steel fencing is one of the best material choices for the Bellarine Peninsula's coastal conditions. The pre-painted steel surface is designed to resist corrosion, fading, and chalking, even in harsh marine environments. The Colorbond coating system includes a zinc-aluminium alloy layer that provides sacrificial protection to the base steel, meaning even if the surface is scratched, the coating continues to protect against rust. For Drysdale properties exposed to direct ocean winds, Colorbond fencing offers exceptional longevity with minimal maintenance.

For homeowners who prefer a natural timber look, the key to making timber fencing work in Drysdale's coastal environment is choosing the right timber species and treatment. Treated pine, pressure-treated to H3 or H4 level, offers good resistance to decay and termites when properly maintained. Hardwood options like ironbark and spotted gum naturally resist rot and insect damage better than softwood species. Whichever timber you choose, applying a quality exterior stain or coating every two to three years is essential to maintain its protective barrier against moisture and UV damage.

Concrete footings are another critical consideration for fencing in the Drysdale area. The Bellarine Peninsula features a mix of soil types, from sandy coastal soils near the beach to heavier clay-based soils further inland. Properly poured concrete footings anchor your fence posts firmly, preventing the leaning and instability that can occur when posts are simply set in the ground. For coastal properties, deep-set concrete footings are especially important to counteract the soil movement that can occur with shifting sandy ground and seasonal moisture changes.

When planning a new fence in Drysdale, it is worth consulting with a local fence contractor who understands the specific challenges of the Bellarine coastal environment. A knowledgeable contractor will recommend the right materials, hardware, and installation methods to ensure your fence withstands the local conditions. At Fencing Geelong & Bellarine, we have over 15 years of experience building fences across the Bellarine Peninsula. We use poured concrete footings, galvanised fittings, and quality timber or Colorbond panels on every project. Contact us today for a free quote on your Drysdale fencing project.

blogPosts.title: How to Choose the Right Fence Contractor in Geelong & Bellarine
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing a fence contractor in Geelong and the Bellarine? Here is what to look for in licensing, experience, materials, and local reputation.
body: Finding the right fence contractor in the Geelong and Bellarine Peninsula area can feel overwhelming, especially with so many options available. Whether you are in Drysdale, Ocean Grove, Leopold, or anywhere across the Bellarine, choosing a contractor who delivers quality workmanship, fair pricing, and reliable service is essential. A well-built fence is a significant investment that protects your property, enhances your curb appeal, and adds value to your home. This guide will help you understand what to look for when selecting a fence contractor in the Geelong and Bellarine region.

The first thing to check when choosing a fence contractor in Geelong or the Bellarine is their licensing and insurance. In Victoria, fencing contractors must hold a valid building licence for work above certain thresholds. Ask to see their licence number and verify it with the Victorian Building Authority. Equally important is public liability insurance, which protects you if anything goes wrong during the project. A reputable fence contractor in Drysdale will have no hesitation providing proof of both their licence and insurance before commencing any work.

Experience in the local area is a crucial factor when selecting a fence contractor on the Bellarine Peninsula. Contractors who regularly work in Drysdale and surrounding suburbs understand the unique challenges of the coastal environment, from soil conditions to wind exposure. They know which materials perform best, which galvanised hardware is necessary for salt-air resistance, and how to set concrete footings for long-term stability. A contractor with 15 or more years of experience on the Bellarine will have encountered and solved every local fencing challenge.

Always ask for detailed, written quotes from any fence contractor you are considering in the Geelong or Bellarine region. A professional quote should itemise all costs, including materials, labour, concrete footings, galvanised fittings, and any council permit fees. Be wary of contractors who provide vague verbal estimates or significantly undercut other quotes, as this often means shortcuts on materials or hidden fees later. At Fencing Geelong & Bellarine, we provide free, fixed-price, written quotes that break down every component so Drysdale and Bellarine homeowners can compare with confidence.

Customer reviews and local reputation are invaluable when choosing a fence contractor in the Bellarine area. Check Google reviews, ask for references from recent jobs, and look for before-and-after photos of completed projects in your suburb. A contractor with consistently positive feedback from Drysdale, Ocean Grove, Leopold, and other Bellarine clients is likely to deliver the same quality for your project. Word-of-mouth recommendations from neighbours and local community groups are also a reliable way to find a trusted fence contractor in the Geelong region.

Finally, consider the range of services and materials a fence contractor offers before making your decision. A full-service contractor who can handle timber fencing, Colorbond fencing, fence repairs, concrete footings, and custom solutions gives you more options for your property. It also means you will not need to engage multiple trades for different aspects of the job. At Fencing Geelong & Bellarine, we provide the complete fencing package across Drysdale, Bellarine, and greater Geelong. Contact us today to arrange a free on-site quote and discover why we are one of the most trusted fence contractors on the Bellarine Peninsula.
